note: One case per rule category (section 9.2). This file is the per-rule test-of-record: check_source must produce exactly the diagnostics a case expects over its source, no more and no fewer. Core conformance (section 9.1) covers the seven construction-time rules HC003, HC006, HC007, HC011, HC-SM01, HC-SM02, HC-SM05; the parse gate HC-SYN holds at every level; HC-P003 is carried as the first structural-rule case. Full and the remaining levels are added as their rules are built (bead honest-framework-4gv).

cases.description: Source that does not parse gates every other rule and reports HC-SYN.

input.source: def f(:

cases.description: A chain() constructed with no links is an empty chain.

input.source:
from honest_type import chain
report = chain()

cases.description: An empty chain is caught when the constructor is imported under an alias (section 3.3).

input.source:
from honest_type import chain as c
report = c()

cases.description: A chain() with links is not empty and fires nothing.

input.source:
from honest_type import chain
report = chain(step_one, step_two)

cases.description: A composed type whose requires names a base type the vocabulary does not declare.

input.source:
from honest_type import vocabulary, composed
v = vocabulary({"digit": {"0", "1"}}, composed_types=[composed("pair", {"missing": "x"}, "digit")])

cases.description: Two Set types in one vocabulary sharing a value overlap, a decidable error.

input.source:
from honest_type import vocabulary
v = vocabulary({"a": {"x", "y"}, "b": {"y", "z"}})

cases.description: Two Set types with no shared value do not overlap.

input.source:
from honest_type import vocabulary
v = vocabulary({"a": {"x", "y"}, "b": {"z"}})

cases.description: A predicate recognizer may be a catch-all; honest-check cannot run it, so it reports info and defers to honest-test.

input.source:
from honest_type import vocabulary
v = vocabulary({"anything": lambda s: True})

cases.description: A transition table names a from-state that is not in the states vocabulary.

input.source:
from honest_type import state_machine
m = state_machine(["idle"], ["go"], {("running", "go"): "idle"}, "idle")

cases.description: A transition table names an event that is not in the events vocabulary.

input.source:
from honest_type import state_machine
m = state_machine(["idle", "run"], ["go"], {("idle", "stop"): "run"}, "idle")

cases.description: The initial state is not in the states vocabulary.

input.source:
from honest_type import state_machine
m = state_machine(["idle"], ["go"], {}, "missing")

cases.description: A state machine whose states, events, transitions and initial all agree fires nothing.

input.source:
from honest_type import state_machine
m = state_machine(["idle", "run"], ["go", "stop"], {("idle", "go"): "run", ("run", "stop"): "idle"}, "idle")

cases.description: A bare class declaration is dishonest: a record is a TypedDict and behaviour is a function.

input.source:
class Report:
    pass

cases.description: Three branches dispatching on one variable's value is an if/elif chain that should be a dict lookup.
A single if that does not dispatch on a value over three branches fires nothing.
An underscore-prefixed instance attribute set in a constructor is hidden instance state.
A constructor that sets no underscore-prefixed instance state fires nothing.
A call to a framework lifecycle hook is dishonest; use server-rendered HTML.

input.source:
def setup():
    useEffect(handler)

cases.description: An ordinary call that is not a lifecycle hook fires nothing.

input.source:
def setup():
    configure(handler)

cases.description: An inner function that captures an enclosing name with nonlocal and mutates it hides state in a closure.
An inner function that captures nothing mutable fires nothing.
A try/except in a non-boundary function swallows a fault that should be raised and caught at the boundary.
A boundary function may catch; the catch belongs at the boundary.
I/O in a non-boundary function touches the world off the boundary.

input.source:
def load(path):
    return open(path).read()

cases.description: A boundary function may perform I/O.
A runtime type check in business logic should be a vocabulary declaration.
Business logic with no runtime type check fires nothing.

input.source:
def classify(x):
    return x + 1

cases.description: A cache decorator without a profiling note has no evidence the cache is warranted.
A cache with a profiling note is dismissed.
Plain honest code fires nothing.
